#!/usr/bin/env bash
# tests/unit/run-limit-precedence-test.sh — run-level wall-clock limit (#1944)
#
# SPEC-2 [code]:
#   _runner_resolve_run_limit_s resolves template max_run_s > ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S >
#   20700; a non-integer or non-positive value in template or env yields
#   disposition misconfigured and the run does not reach the dispatch loop.
#
# SPEC-5 [no-code]:
#   The limit is resolved from template, env, or constant only; scripts/lib/
#   stage-limits.sh and core/pipeline/runner.sh contain no reference to
#   GITHUB_ACTIONS, CI, or any platform-specific variable in the new code.
#
# SPEC-6 [no-code]:
#   ADR-025 names timed_out in its word vocabulary with ## Enforced by entries
#   citing the new tests; ADR-054 gains a §11 for the run-level limit with
#   ## Enforced by; config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt no longer lists
#   ADR-054-stage-contract.md.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "run-limit-precedence: max_run_s resolution + platform-free + ADR alignment (#1944)"
setup_test_env "run-limit-precedence"

RUNNER="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"
STAGE_LIMITS="$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/stage-limits.sh"

# ─── SPEC-2: _runner_resolve_run_limit_s ────────────────────────────────────

print_test_section "[#1944/SPEC-2] _runner_resolve_run_limit_s is defined in stage-limits.sh"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/stage-limits.sh
source "$STAGE_LIMITS" 2>/dev/null || true

if declare -F _runner_resolve_run_limit_s >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-2] _runner_resolve_run_limit_s is defined in stage-limits.sh"
else
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-2] _runner_resolve_run_limit_s is defined in stage-limits.sh" \
        "function not found after sourcing scripts/lib/stage-limits.sh"
fi

print_test_section "[#1944/SPEC-2] precedence: template max_run_s > ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S > 20700"

if declare -F _runner_resolve_run_limit_s >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    # Case 1: no template value, no env → falls back to default 20700
    _RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S=""
    template_max_run_s() { printf ''; }
    unset ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S
    _runner_resolve_run_limit_s 2>/dev/null || true
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] no template, no env → default 20700" "20700" "${_RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S:-}"

    # Case 2: env only → uses env
    _RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S=""
    template_max_run_s() { printf ''; }
    ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S=3600
    _runner_resolve_run_limit_s 2>/dev/null || true
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] env ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S=3600 used when no template value" "3600" "${_RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S:-}"
    unset ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S

    # Case 3: template value > env → template wins
    _RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S=""
    template_max_run_s() { printf '7200'; }
    ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S=3600
    _runner_resolve_run_limit_s 2>/dev/null || true
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] template value wins over ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S" "7200" "${_RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S:-}"
    unset ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S

    # Case 4: template value only (no env) → template wins over default
    _RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S=""
    template_max_run_s() { printf '1800'; }
    unset ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S
    _runner_resolve_run_limit_s 2>/dev/null || true
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] template value wins over default" "1800" "${_RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S:-}"
else
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-2] precedence checks skipped — function not found" "missing implementation"
fi

print_test_section "[#1944/SPEC-2] non-integer / non-positive → misconfigured, rc=1"

if declare -F _runner_resolve_run_limit_s >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    # Non-integer in template
    _RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S=""
    template_max_run_s() { printf 'not-a-number'; }
    unset ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S
    _rc2=0
    _runner_resolve_run_limit_s 2>/dev/null || _rc2=$?
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] non-integer template value → rc=1" "1" "$_rc2"

    # Non-positive (zero) in template
    _RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S=""
    template_max_run_s() { printf '0'; }
    unset ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S
    _rc2=0
    _runner_resolve_run_limit_s 2>/dev/null || _rc2=$?
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] template value=0 → rc=1" "1" "$_rc2"

    # Negative in template
    _RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S=""
    template_max_run_s() { printf -- '-5'; }
    unset ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S
    _rc2=0
    _runner_resolve_run_limit_s 2>/dev/null || _rc2=$?
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] negative template value → rc=1" "1" "$_rc2"

    # Non-integer in ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S
    _RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S=""
    template_max_run_s() { printf ''; }
    ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S="thirty"
    _rc2=0
    _runner_resolve_run_limit_s 2>/dev/null || _rc2=$?
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] non-integer ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S → rc=1" "1" "$_rc2"
    unset ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S

    # Non-positive in ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S
    _RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S=""
    template_max_run_s() { printf ''; }
    ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S=0
    _rc2=0
    _runner_resolve_run_limit_s 2>/dev/null || _rc2=$?
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S=0 → rc=1" "1" "$_rc2"
    unset ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S
else
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-2] validation checks skipped — function not found" "missing implementation"
fi

# ─── SPEC-2: template_max_run_s() from the real template.sh ─────────────────
# This section sources the REAL template.sh to test its template_max_run_s()
# function directly. If template.sh is reverted (function removed), the
# assert_fail below fires — making template.sh testable.
print_test_section "[#1944/SPEC-2] template_max_run_s() reads max_run_s from template YAML (real function)"
TEMPLATE_SH="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/template.sh"

# shellcheck source=../../core/pipeline/template.sh
source "$TEMPLATE_SH" 2>/dev/null || true

# Build two YAML fixtures: one WITH max_run_s, one WITHOUT
_tpl_yaml="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/max-run-test.yaml"
cat > "$_tpl_yaml" <<'EOF'
id: max-run-test
max_run_s: 3600
extends: simple
EOF

_tpl_none="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/no-max-run.yaml"
cat > "$_tpl_none" <<'EOF'
id: no-max-run-test
extends: simple
EOF

if declare -F template_max_run_s >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    # Real function from template.sh: must extract the value from the YAML.
    _TPL_SOURCE_FILE="$_tpl_yaml"
    _tmr="$(template_max_run_s 2>/dev/null || true)"
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] template_max_run_s() returns max_run_s value from YAML" "3600" "$_tmr"

    # When max_run_s is absent, function returns empty (no override)
    _TPL_SOURCE_FILE="$_tpl_none"
    _tmr_empty="$(template_max_run_s 2>/dev/null || true)"
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] template_max_run_s() returns empty when max_run_s absent" "" "$_tmr_empty"
    unset _TPL_SOURCE_FILE
else
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-2] template_max_run_s() defined in core/pipeline/template.sh" \
        "function not found after sourcing template.sh — implementation missing or template.sh reverted"
fi

print_test_section "[#1944/SPEC-2] misconfigured run (invalid ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S): runner rejects before dispatch"
# Run the actual runner with an invalid ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S; it must exit non-zero

cleanup_test_env

# scripts/lib/lint-test-errexit.sh — #2252 G
#
# A test file that runs without stop-on-error (its first `set -…` line has no
# `e`) must not turn it on later: from that line every assertion that expects a
# non-zero rc kills the file instead of being checked. #1844's test-author
# wrapped a call in `set +e … set -e` inside a `set -uo pipefail` file and the
# next expected rc=1 aborted it. A file that starts with -e may toggle it.
#
# Usage: bash scripts/lib/lint-test-errexit.sh [root]   (default: the repo)
# Exit:  0 = clean; 1 = at least one offending file.
set -euo pipefail

_LTE_ROOT="${1:-$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)}"
_bad=0
while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
    [[ "$f" == */legacy-DoNotUse/* ]] && continue
    # One awk pass: the header is the first `set -<flags>` line of the file's own
    # shell; heredoc bodies are skipped — a fixture script written by the test is
    # not the test's own shell (its `set -e` is the fixture's business).
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r ln header; do
        [[ -n "$ln" ]] || continue
        echo "lint-test-errexit: ${f#"$_LTE_ROOT"/}:$ln turns stop-on-error on in a file that runs without it (header: ${header:-none}) — an expected non-zero rc after this line kills the file; use 'cmd || rc=\$?' instead" >&2
        _bad=$((_bad + 1))
    done < <(awk '
        doc != "" { t = $0; sub(/^\t+/, "", t); if (t == doc) doc = ""; next }
        /^[[:space:]]*#/ { next }
        # The line itself is judged BEFORE a heredoc it opens hides what follows:
        # a set -e on the opening line belongs to the test shell (review #2253).
        !seen && /^set -[a-zA-Z]+/ {
            seen = 1; hdr = $0; f = $2; sub(/^-/, "", f)
            haserr = (f ~ /e/); next
        }
        seen && !haserr && /^[[:space:]]*set -[a-zA-Z]*e[a-zA-Z]*([[:space:]]|$)/ { print NR "\t" hdr }
        {
            line = $0
            if (match(line, /<<-?[[:space:]]*["\047]?[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*["\047]?/)) {
                d = substr(line, RSTART, RLENGTH); sub(/^<<-?[[:space:]]*/, "", d); gsub(/["\047]/, "", d)

            }
        }
    ' "$f" 2>/dev/null)

    echo "lint-test-errexit: $_bad file(s) switch stop-on-error on mid-file" >&2
    exit 1
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Integration: run-level wall-clock limit with watchdog (#1944)
#
# SPEC-1 [code]: a run whose wall-clock time exceeds max_run_s ends with
#   pipeline status timed_out in pipeline-state.json and pipeline.end event
#   carrying status=timed_out, the in-flight stage, and limit_s; the watchdog
#   fires even when the engine is idle between dispatches (not only inside a
#   stage); a process that ignores TERM is dead within TERM + 10 s; release and
#   persist execute on every timed-out exit path.
#
# Phases:
#   P1 — basic timeout: slow stage hits the watchdog; status=timed_out, event
#        fields correct; runner exits non-zero within the limit
#   P2 — idle between dispatches: fast-one completes before watchdog fires;
#        watchdog fires while fast-two is sleeping; fast-one being in "complete"
#        state proves the watchdog runs independently of stage dispatch state
#   P3 — TERM-ignore: a stage that traps and ignores SIGTERM is dead within
#        TERM + 10 s (KILL escalation)
#   P4 — release and persist run: always_run release + persist stages execute
#        on every timed-out exit path
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
RUNNER="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "run-timed-out: wall-clock limit watchdog fires and ends run correctly (#1944)"
setup_test_env "run-timed-out"
export ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn

PLUGINS_ROOT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins"
STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state"
EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events"
EVENTS_JSONL="$EVENTS_DIR/events.jsonl"
export ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$PLUGINS_ROOT"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$EVENTS_DIR"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$EVENTS_JSONL"
export ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json"
export ZBUILD_MODELS_FILE="$REPO_ROOT/config/models.json"
export ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=0
export ZBUILD_SCOPE_OVERRIDE=1
mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR" "$EVENTS_DIR" "$HOME/.zbuild"
printf '%s' "bootstrap" > "$HOME/.zbuild/scope-override-token"

# ── Shared overlay repo ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
OVERLAY_REPO="$(setup_git_temp_repo run-timed-out-overlay)"
mkdir -p "$OVERLAY_REPO/.zbuild/templates"

# Single-stage template: one slow stage (the main timeout victim)
cat > "$OVERLAY_REPO/.zbuild/templates/timeout-single.yaml" <<'EOF'
id: timeout-single
extends: simple
stages:
  - id: slow-stage
    gate: auto
    io:
      destinations: [file]
      tail_lines: 50
    router:
      timeout_s: 120
      max_turns: 0
EOF

# Two-stage template: fast-one is instant; fast-two blocks for a long time
cat > "$OVERLAY_REPO/.zbuild/templates/timeout-two-stage.yaml" <<'EOF'
id: timeout-two-stage
extends: simple
stages:
  - id: fast-one
    gate: auto
    io:
      destinations: [file]
      tail_lines: 50
  - id: fast-two
    gate: auto
    io:
      destinations: [file]
      tail_lines: 50
EOF

# Always-run (release + persist) template: flow stage + always_run release + persist
cat > "$OVERLAY_REPO/.zbuild/templates/timeout-with-release.yaml" <<'EOF'
id: timeout-with-release
extends: simple
flow:
  - outcome

always_run:
  - release
  - persist-stage

outcome:
  gate: auto
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 50

release:
  gate: auto
  roles: [teardown]
  router:
    timeout_s: 30
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 50

persist-stage:
  gate: auto
  roles: [persist]
  router:
    timeout_s: 30
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 50
EOF

# Commit the templates into the overlay repo so the runner can find them
(cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && git add .zbuild && git commit -q -m "add timeout test templates") >/dev/null 2>&1

# ── P1: basic timeout — slow stage, status=timed_out ───────────────────────

# Stage that sleeps far longer than max_run_s
mock_plugin_factory "slow-stage" "agent" 0 >/dev/null
SLOW_STAGE_STARTED="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/slow-stage-started"
cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/slow-stage/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
slow_stage_run() {
    : > "${SLOW_STAGE_STARTED}"
    sleep 120
    $(mock_v2_result_line slow-stage)
    return 0
}
PLUG

export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$STATE_DIR"
print_test_section "P1: slow stage timeout — status=timed_out written to pipeline-state.json"

# Run with ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S=2 (2 seconds); wrap in timeout 25s to prevent hanging
# before implementation (no watchdog → stage sleeps forever → outer timeout kills it)
p1_rc=0
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S=2 timeout 25 bash "$RUNNER" \
    --template timeout-single --goal "run-timed-out test p1" ) \
    >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/p1.stdout" 2>"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/p1.stderr" \
    || p1_rc=$?

STATE_FILE="$STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json"

# pipeline-state.json must exist and have status=timed_out
if [[ ! -f "$STATE_FILE" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-1] P1: pipeline-state.json written" "state file not found"
else
    _p1_status="$(jq -r '.status // empty' "$STATE_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-1] P1: pipeline-state.json status=timed_out" "timed_out" "$_p1_status"
fi

print_test_section "P1: pipeline.end event fields — status=timed_out, stage, limit_s"

if [[ ! -f "$EVENTS_JSONL" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-1] P1: events.jsonl written" "events file not found"
else
    # Event: pipeline.end with status=timed_out
    _p1_end_event="$(jq -c 'select(.type=="pipeline.end" and .data.status=="timed_out")' \
        "$EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null | tail -1)"
    if [[ -n "$_p1_end_event" ]]; then
        assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-1] P1: pipeline.end status=timed_out event emitted"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-1] P1: pipeline.end status=timed_out event emitted" \
            "no such event in $(wc -l < "$EVENTS_JSONL") events"
    fi

    # The event must carry the in-flight stage name
    _p1_stage="$(jq -r 'select(.type=="pipeline.end" and .data.status=="timed_out") | .data.stage // empty' \
        "$EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null | tail -1)"
    if [[ -n "$_p1_stage" ]]; then
        assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-1] P1: pipeline.end event carries in-flight stage (stage=$_p1_stage)"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-1] P1: pipeline.end event carries in-flight stage" \
            "stage field empty in timed_out pipeline.end event"
    fi

    # The event must carry limit_s (the max_run_s value that was applied)
    _p1_limit="$(jq -r 'select(.type=="pipeline.end" and .data.status=="timed_out") | .data.limit_s // empty' \
        "$EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null | tail -1)"
    if [[ -n "$_p1_limit" && "$_p1_limit" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
        assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-1] P1: pipeline.end event carries limit_s=$_p1_limit"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-1] P1: pipeline.end event carries limit_s" \
            "limit_s field absent or non-numeric in timed_out pipeline.end event"
    fi
fi

# ── P2: idle between dispatches — watchdog fires independently of stage state ─
print_test_section "P2: watchdog fires even when engine is idle between dispatches"

# Reset state/events for fresh run

mock_plugin_factory "fast-two" "agent" 0 >/dev/null

# max_run_s=3: watchdog fires 3s into the run. fast-one completes in < 1s.

# the watchdog ran independently — it did not need a stage to be dispatching.
# If the watchdog fired BEFORE fast-one completed, fast-one's status would not be
# "complete", and the assertion below would fail.
FAST_TWO_STARTED="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/fast-two-started"
cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/fast-one/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
fast_one_run() {
    $(mock_v2_result_line fast-one)
    return 0
}
PLUG
cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/fast-two/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
fast_two_run() {
    : > "${FAST_TWO_STARTED}"
    sleep 30
    $(mock_v2_result_line fast-two)
    return 0
}
PLUG

p2_rc=0
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S=3 timeout 25 bash "$RUNNER" \
    --template timeout-two-stage --goal "run-timed-out test p2" ) \
    >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/p2.stdout" 2>"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/p2.stderr" \
    || p2_rc=$?

assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-1] P2: runner exits non-zero" "1" "$p2_rc"

if [[ -f "$STATE_FILE" ]]; then
    _p2_status="$(jq -r '.status // empty' "$STATE_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-1] P2: pipeline status=timed_out (watchdog fires regardless of dispatch state)" \
        "timed_out" "$_p2_status"

    # fast-one MUST have completed before the watchdog fired: its status must be
    # "complete". This is the falsifiable check — if the watchdog fired before
    # fast-one completed, fast-one's status would not be "complete" and this fails.
    # Stage names are stored with their literal name (hyphenated) as the key.
    _p2_fast_one="$(jq -r '.stage_statuses["fast-one"] // empty' "$STATE_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if [[ "$_p2_fast_one" == "complete" ]]; then
        assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-1] P2: fast-one completed before watchdog fired (watchdog fires independently)"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-1] P2: fast-one completed before watchdog fired" \

    fi
else
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-1] P2: pipeline-state.json written" "state file not found"
fi

# ── P3: TERM-ignore → KILL within TERM + 10s ────────────────────────────────

        fi
    fi
fi

# ── P4: release AND persist stages run on timed-out exit path ───────────────
print_test_section "P4: always_run release and persist stages execute on timed-out exit path"

rm -f "$STATE_FILE" "$EVENTS_JSONL"

mock_plugin_factory "outcome"       "agent" 0 "" ""        >/dev/null

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Integration: resumed run after timed_out uses a fresh watchdog (#1944)
#
# SPEC-4 [code]: a run resumed after a timed_out end is not stopped
#   immediately — its watchdog is armed from the resumed run's wall-clock
#   start, not the original run's.
#
# Phases:
#   P1 (unit):        get_resume_recommendation(timed_out) = manual_resume_only;
#                     not auto_resume and not fresh_start.
#   P2 (unit):        _runner_resolve_run_limit_s is defined in stage-limits.sh
#                     — the function that arms the watchdog on every invocation,
#                     including --resume. Absent before the implementation.
#   P3 (integration): a run resumed (--force) after a timed_out state with a
#                     generous max_run_s completes normally — not stopped
#                     immediately, proving the watchdog was armed from the
#                     resumed run's wall-clock start.
#   P4 (integration): a run resumed with a tight max_run_s and a slow stage
#                     DOES time out — proving the watchdog is actually ARMED
#                     on the resumed run (not absent or disarmed). Together
#                     P3 + P4 establish "armed from the resumed run's start":
#                     P3 shows it doesn't fire too early, P4 shows it fires
#                     when the resumed run's OWN limit is genuinely exceeded.
#
# Why the test fails before implementation:
#   P1: get_resume_recommendation has no timed_out case; the `*` catch-all
#       returns fresh_start, not manual_resume_only. The assert_eq fails.
#   P2: _runner_resolve_run_limit_s is not yet defined. The assert_fail fires.

setup_test_env "resume-after-run-timeout"

    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-4] P1: get_resume_recommendation(timed_out) = manual_resume_only" \

    >/dev/null 2>&1

RESUME_STATE_FILE="$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json"

    >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/p3.stdout" 2>"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/p3.stderr" \

    fi

    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-4] P3: pipeline-state.json accessible after resumed run" \

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# scripts/lib/stage-limits.sh — the limits a stage's model calls run under.
3	#
4	# One copy, two readers: the router enforces these numbers on every call
5	# (core/router/route.sh) and the engine states them to the stage in its rules
6	# (scripts/lib/stage-prompt.sh, ADR-067 §8). A stage told a different budget
7	# from the one it is killed at works until it is killed.
8	#
9	# Sourced library: inherits the caller's shell options; do NOT add set -euo.
10	[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_STAGE_LIMITS_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
11	_ZBUILD_STAGE_LIMITS_LOADED=1
12	
13	if ! declare -F manifest_router_knob >/dev/null 2>&1; then
14	    # shellcheck source=../../core/plugin-registry/manifest-router-budget.sh
15	    source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)/core/plugin-registry/manifest-router-budget.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
16	fi
17	
18	# ─── _route_manifest_knob <knob> — ADR-017 §11 (#1816) manifest layer ───────
19	# The dispatched plugin's OWN declared default, read from its manifest via the
20	# dispatch identity the engine exports at plugin_hook_call (ZBUILD_PLUGIN_DIR,
21	# ADR-054 §3 / #1862). Empty whenever there is no dispatch, no manifest, no
22	# declaration — or a declaration this router cannot use.
23	#
24	# Out-of-range and non-numeric values are IGNORED here, not fatal: the loud
25	# gate is validate_manifest at load, and a plugin that got past it with a bad
26	# value must fall back to the constant rather than hand the router a 0-second
27	# timeout. Fail-safe on the hot path, fail-loud at the boundary.
28	_route_manifest_knob() {
29	    local knob="$1"
30	    local dir="${ZBUILD_PLUGIN_DIR:-}"
31	    [[ -n "$dir" && -f "$dir/manifest.yaml" ]] || return 0
32	    declare -F manifest_router_knob >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
33	    local v; v="$(manifest_router_knob "$dir/manifest.yaml" "$knob" 2>/dev/null || true)"
34	    [[ "$v" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
35	    local range; range="$(_manifest_router_range "$knob" 2>/dev/null || true)"
36	    [[ -n "$range" ]] || return 0
37	    local min="${range% *}" max="${range#* }"
38	    [[ "$v" -ge "$min" && "$v" -le "$max" ]] || return 0
39	    printf '%s' "$v"
40	}
41	
42	# ─── _route_resolve_knob — ADR-017 (#455) precedence chokepoint ──────────────
43	# Generic helper: future knobs (tier_default, budget_usd, model_override) reuse
44	# this. Accessor returns per-stage value or empty; env_var supplies session-wide
45	# fallback; manifest_knob (#1816) names the plugin's own declared default; the
46	# compile-time constant is the floor:
47	#
48	#   template accessor  >  env var  >  manifest config.router.*  >  constant
49	#
50	# The manifest sits BELOW env and template because it is a default, not an
51	# override: a flow may right-size a stage for a fast lane, and the operator
52	# escape hatch must still beat both. It sits ABOVE the constant because that is
53	# what the constant always was — a default nobody could state per stage.
54	_route_resolve_knob() {
55	    local accessor_fn="$1" env_var="$2" default_val="$3"
56	    local override_event="${4:-router.timeout.override_ignored}"
57	    local manifest_knob="${5:-}"
58	    local v=""
59	    if [[ -n "${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}" ]] && declare -F "$accessor_fn" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
60	        v="$($accessor_fn "$ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
61	    fi
62	    if [[ -n "$v" ]]; then
63	        # If env var ALSO set and differs, emit override-ignored event for audit.
64	        # A manifest value losing to template or env is NOT this case: a default
65	        # being replaced is the design, and eventing it would make every
66	        # declaring plugin noisy on every dispatch.
67	        local env_val="${!env_var:-}"
68	        if [[ -n "$env_val" && "$env_val" != "$v" ]]; then
69	            eb_emit_event "$override_event" \
70	                "stage=${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}" \
71	                "env_var=$env_var" \
72	                "env_value=$env_val" \
73	                "applied=$v" 2>/dev/null || true
74	        fi
75	        printf '%s\n' "$v"; return 0
76	    fi
77	    local env_v="${!env_var:-}"
78	    if [[ -n "$env_v" ]]; then
79	        printf '%s\n' "$env_v"; return 0
80	    fi
81	    if [[ -n "$manifest_knob" ]]; then
82	        local mv; mv="$(_route_manifest_knob "$manifest_knob")"
83	        if [[ -n "$mv" ]]; then
84	            printf '%s\n' "$mv"; return 0
85	        fi
86	    fi
87	    printf '%s\n' "$default_val"
88	}
89	
90	# Concrete: per-stage router.timeout_s > $ZBUILD_ROUTER_TIMEOUT >
91	# manifest config.router.timeout_s > 300s default.
92	_route_resolve_timeout() {
93	    _route_resolve_knob template_stage_router_timeout ZBUILD_ROUTER_TIMEOUT 300 \

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/lib/stage-limits.sh — the limits a stage's model calls run under.
#
# One copy, two readers: the router enforces these numbers on every call
# (core/router/route.sh) and the engine states them to the stage in its rules
# (scripts/lib/stage-prompt.sh, ADR-067 §8). A stage told a different budget
# from the one it is killed at works until it is killed.
#
# Sourced library: inherits the caller's shell options; do NOT add set -euo.
[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_STAGE_LIMITS_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_STAGE_LIMITS_LOADED=1

if ! declare -F manifest_router_knob >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    # shellcheck source=../../core/plugin-registry/manifest-router-budget.sh
    source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)/core/plugin-registry/manifest-router-budget.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
fi

# ─── _route_manifest_knob <knob> — ADR-017 §11 (#1816) manifest layer ───────
# The dispatched plugin's OWN declared default, read from its manifest via the
# dispatch identity the engine exports at plugin_hook_call (ZBUILD_PLUGIN_DIR,
# ADR-054 §3 / #1862). Empty whenever there is no dispatch, no manifest, no
# declaration — or a declaration this router cannot use.
#
# Out-of-range and non-numeric values are IGNORED here, not fatal: the loud
# gate is validate_manifest at load, and a plugin that got past it with a bad
# value must fall back to the constant rather than hand the router a 0-second
# timeout. Fail-safe on the hot path, fail-loud at the boundary.
_route_manifest_knob() {
    local knob="$1"
    local dir="${ZBUILD_PLUGIN_DIR:-}"
    [[ -n "$dir" && -f "$dir/manifest.yaml" ]] || return 0
    declare -F manifest_router_knob >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
    local v; v="$(manifest_router_knob "$dir/manifest.yaml" "$knob" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    [[ "$v" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
    local range; range="$(_manifest_router_range "$knob" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    [[ -n "$range" ]] || return 0
    local min="${range% *}" max="${range#* }"
    [[ "$v" -ge "$min" && "$v" -le "$max" ]] || return 0
    printf '%s' "$v"
}

# ─── _route_resolve_knob — ADR-017 (#455) precedence chokepoint ──────────────
# Generic helper: future knobs (tier_default, budget_usd, model_override) reuse
# this. Accessor returns per-stage value or empty; env_var supplies session-wide
# fallback; manifest_knob (#1816) names the plugin's own declared default; the
# compile-time constant is the floor:
#
#   template accessor  >  env var  >  manifest config.router.*  >  constant
#
# The manifest sits BELOW env and template because it is a default, not an
# override: a flow may right-size a stage for a fast lane, and the operator
# escape hatch must still beat both. It sits ABOVE the constant because that is
# what the constant always was — a default nobody could state per stage.
_route_resolve_knob() {
    local accessor_fn="$1" env_var="$2" default_val="$3"
    local override_event="${4:-router.timeout.override_ignored}"
    local manifest_knob="${5:-}"
    local v=""
    if [[ -n "${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}" ]] && declare -F "$accessor_fn" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        v="$($accessor_fn "$ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    fi
    if [[ -n "$v" ]]; then
        # If env var ALSO set and differs, emit override-ignored event for audit.
        # A manifest value losing to template or env is NOT this case: a default
        # being replaced is the design, and eventing it would make every
        # declaring plugin noisy on every dispatch.
        local env_val="${!env_var:-}"
        if [[ -n "$env_val" && "$env_val" != "$v" ]]; then
            eb_emit_event "$override_event" \
                "stage=${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}" \
                "env_var=$env_var" \
                "env_value=$env_val" \
                "applied=$v" 2>/dev/null || true
        fi
        printf '%s\n' "$v"; return 0
    fi
    local env_v="${!env_var:-}"
    if [[ -n "$env_v" ]]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$env_v"; return 0
    fi
    if [[ -n "$manifest_knob" ]]; then
        local mv; mv="$(_route_manifest_knob "$manifest_knob")"
        if [[ -n "$mv" ]]; then
            printf '%s\n' "$mv"; return 0
        fi
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "$default_val"
}

# Concrete: per-stage router.timeout_s > $ZBUILD_ROUTER_TIMEOUT >
# manifest config.router.timeout_s > 300s default.
_route_resolve_timeout() {
    _route_resolve_knob template_stage_router_timeout ZBUILD_ROUTER_TIMEOUT 300 \
        router.timeout.override_ignored timeout_s
}

# ADR-018 (#466): per-stage router.max_turns > $ZBUILD_ROUTER_MAX_TURNS > 25 default.
# ADR-029 G3 (#812): when the cycle orchestrator detects a router timeout for
# this stage, it sets ZBUILD_ROUTER_MAX_TURNS_OVERRIDE so the next dispatch
# of the same stage uses an escalated budget (+50%, capped at 2× base). The
# override wins over the per-stage template AND the env knob because that's
# the entire point — escalation must beat the static config that already
# proved too small.
_route_resolve_max_turns() {
    if [[ "${ZBUILD_ROUTER_MAX_TURNS_OVERRIDE:-}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
        printf '%s' "$ZBUILD_ROUTER_MAX_TURNS_OVERRIDE"
        return 0
    fi
    _route_resolve_knob template_stage_router_max_turns ZBUILD_ROUTER_MAX_TURNS 25 \
        router.max_turns.override_ignored max_turns
}

# ADR-018 Amendment N (#762): when max_turns resolves to the 0 sentinel,
# classify which source set it (template > env > manifest > default) for
# telemetry. Emits `template`, `env`, `manifest` (#1816), or `default`. The
# `default` branch is currently unreachable (compile-time default is 25, not 0)
# but kept for forward compatibility if the default ever changes.
# Copilot review #764: compare numerically so "00", "000" etc. (accepted
# by the ^[0-9]+$ validator) classify correctly.
_route_classify_max_turns_source() {
    local _tpl_val=""
    if [[ -n "${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}" ]] \
        && command -v template_stage_router_max_turns >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        _tpl_val="$(template_stage_router_max_turns "$ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    fi
    local _mf_val; _mf_val="$(_route_manifest_knob max_turns)"
    if [[ "$_tpl_val" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ "$_tpl_val" -eq 0 ]]; then
        printf '%s' "template"
    elif [[ "${ZBUILD_ROUTER_MAX_TURNS:-}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ "${ZBUILD_ROUTER_MAX_TURNS}" -eq 0 ]]; then
        printf '%s' "env"
    elif [[ "$_mf_val" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ "$_mf_val" -eq 0 ]]; then
        # #1816: a plugin that declares `max_turns: 0` owns that sentinel. Left
        # unclassified it would be recorded as `default`, which is the one thing
        # it is not — the record would name a source that declared nothing.
        printf '%s' "manifest"
    else
        printf '%s' "default"
    fi
}

# ADR-018 (#467): per-stage router.max_iterations > $ZBUILD_ROUTER_MAX_ITERATIONS > 10 default.
_route_resolve_max_iterations() {
    _route_resolve_knob template_stage_router_max_iterations ZBUILD_ROUTER_MAX_ITERATIONS 10 \
        router.max_iterations.override_ignored
}

# ADR-029 (#1230): per-stage router.retries > $ZBUILD_ROUTER_RETRIES > 0 default.
# The count of retry-on-timeout (rc=124) attempts BEFORE the verbatim-124
# fallback. Default 0 (opt-in). Honored by BOTH leaf paths — single-shot
# (_route_call_claude) and agentic-loop (route_to_model_loop) — so every leaf
# node respects the knob wherever it sits. Out-of-range values (validator
# already bounds template 0..10; env is unbounded) clamp to 0 fail-safe.
_route_resolve_retries() {
    local v; v="$(_route_resolve_knob template_stage_router_retries ZBUILD_ROUTER_RETRIES 0 \
        router.retries.override_ignored retries)"
    if [[ "$v" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ "$v" -ge 0 ]] && [[ "$v" -le 10 ]]; then
        printf '%s' "$v"
    else
        printf '0'
    fi
}

# ADR-054 §11 (#1944): per-run wall-clock limit.
# Priority: template max_run_s > ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S > 20700 s default.
# A non-integer or non-positive value in either source is refused (rc=1).
# Result written to global _RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S.
_runner_resolve_run_limit_s() {
    local _tpl_v="" _env_v=""
    # Template layer — calls template_max_run_s() when available.
    if declare -F template_max_run_s >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        _tpl_v="$(template_max_run_s 2>/dev/null || true)"
    fi
    if [[ -n "$_tpl_v" ]]; then
        if [[ "$_tpl_v" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ "$_tpl_v" -gt 0 ]]; then
            _RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S="$_tpl_v"
            return 0
        else
            printf 'run limit misconfigured: template max_run_s must be a positive integer (got: %s)\n' \
                "$_tpl_v" >&2
            return 1
        fi
    fi
    # Env layer.
    _env_v="${ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S:-}"
    if [[ -n "$_env_v" ]]; then
        if [[ "$_env_v" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ "$_env_v" -gt 0 ]]; then
            _RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S="$_env_v"
            return 0
        else
            printf 'run limit misconfigured: ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S must be a positive integer (got: %s)\n' \
                "$_env_v" >&2
            return 1
        fi
    fi
    # Default.
    _RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S=20700
    return 0
}

        if [[ $_r_cyc_count -gt 0 ]]; then
            local _fs_cycle_id="" _cyc
            for _cyc in "${_TPL_CYCLES[@]}"; do
                local _safe="${_cyc//-/_}"
                local _stages_var="_TPL_CYCLE_STAGES_${_safe}"
                local _stages_csv="${!_stages_var:-}"
                local IFS_save="$IFS"; IFS=','
                # shellcheck disable=SC2206
                local -a _cs=($_stages_csv)
                IFS="$IFS_save"
                local _cs_s
                for _cs_s in "${_cs[@]}"; do
                    [[ "$_cs_s" == "$from_stage" ]] && { _fs_cycle_id="$_cyc"; break 2; }
                done
            done
            # Check "after a cycle" too — locate from_stage position and any
            # cycle position in active_stages, reject if any cycle position
            # is strictly less.
            local _after_cycle=0
            if [[ -z "$_fs_cycle_id" ]]; then
                local _fs_pos=-1 _i
                for _i in "${!active_stages[@]}"; do
                    [[ "${active_stages[$_i]}" == "$from_stage" ]] && _fs_pos=$_i && break
                done
                for _cyc in "${_TPL_CYCLES[@]}"; do
                    local _safe2="${_cyc//-/_}"
                    local _sv2="_TPL_CYCLE_STAGES_${_safe2}"
                    local _scsv2="${!_sv2:-}"
                    local _first_stage="${_scsv2%%,*}"
                    local _cpos=-1
                    for _i in "${!active_stages[@]}"; do
                        [[ "${active_stages[$_i]}" == "$_first_stage" ]] && _cpos=$_i && break
                    done
                    if [[ $_cpos -ge 0 && $_fs_pos -gt $_cpos ]]; then
                        _after_cycle=1; break
                    fi
                done
            fi
            if [[ -n "$_fs_cycle_id" || $_after_cycle -eq 1 ]]; then
                eb_emit_event "pipeline.from_stage.rejected" \
                    "reason=inside_cycle_or_after" "from_stage=$from_stage" \
                    "cycle_id=${_fs_cycle_id:-}" 2>/dev/null || true
                error "--from-stage '$from_stage' lands inside or after a cycle ('${_fs_cycle_id:-after-cycle}') — refused. Resume the cycle from its first stage or omit --from-stage."
                return 1
            fi
        fi
